newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo takes currency boost in 9-mo '96.
newsitem.headline: Volvo takes currency boost in 9-mo '96.

text.p: Swedish automotive group AB Volvo reported on Wednesday a 12 percent rise in profits for the first nine months of the year, helped by a 600 million crown ($91.2 million) boost to profits at operating level from currency movements.
Volvo's pre-tax profit of 12.03 billion crowns came in below market expectations, with a Reuter poll of analysts finding a market consensus of 12.79 billion crowns.

Sales for the period fell 12 percent to 113.64 billion crowns from the 129.12 billion reported in the same 1995 period, largely due to a 14 drop in sales from the truck division to 32.71 billion crowns.
No immediate recovery was in sight for truck sales, and Volvo noted that order books were 40 percent lower than at the same time last year, largely due to falling demand in North and South America.
The truck division reported an operating profit of just 413 million crowns, down from 4.03 billion in the same 1995 period.
Operating profits from the car division fell to 573 million crowns from the nine-month 1995 level of 1.93 billion.
Car sales fared slightly better and fell just four percent to 59.83 billion crowns.
Volvo described this as "unsatisfactory" but noted that sales of the division's new S40/V40 series were in line with expectations and the model was contributing to group profits.
The main contributor to earnings for the first nine months of the year was capital gains of 8.21 billion crowns on the sale of shareholdings during the period.
Of this, Volvo's divestment of its holding in drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn, Inc., accounted for a capital gain of 7.8 billion, Volvo said.
